title: One member buys Plus and the partner expects it immediately
preconditions: A and B are active members of one space on the Free plan.
B keeps the app open and checks storage limits.

actions.note: A completes a verified Plus purchase.
B checks the current storage limit.

expected_behavior: Plus is Space-level; both members read the same authoritative entitlement row.
B observes the higher media ceiling after the entitlement is applied, not merely after the store sheet closes.
A failed or delayed webhook does not grant Plus on the client alone.
candidate_failure_modes: B sees Free limits indefinitely with no explanation.
The client grants Plus from local purchase state while the server still says Free.
A second purchase is required for the partner.
existing_test_coverage: packages/api/src/__tests__/routes/session-plus.test.ts:141 — valid webhook activates Plus for the purchaser Space; partner reads the same state

observed_code_behavior: Plus is a Space-level entitlement: one row is shared by both active members.
The Free media ceiling is 250 MiB and the Plus ceiling is 5 GiB; future-letter allowance differs by plan.
The backend entitlement row is authoritative; client local purchase state cannot grant features.
Verified webhook deliveries are deduplicated and stale events cannot regress a newer state.
Us and Memories are intentionally separate destinations; sky photos are not dated memories.
Free and Plus see the same relationship home.

hypothetical_user_behavior: A fictional participant (Jules Park) said: "We are auditing Aoi for things that do not need to exist. Walk through Plus and storage as you actually used them: the paywall, plan explanation, storage meter, manage-subscription link, upgrade prompts, feature gates, and every line of copy around them. For each one, ask out loud: "Why does this even exist?" Then say what would break if it were removed, and what it cost you. Name the three most useless things and the one thing you would keep. Do not propose a redesign; remove."

A fictional participant (Jules Park) said: "Did this out loud, twice — once with reduce-motion on, once off. Findings.

Three things that should not exist:
1) The animated storage meter. On mount it counts up from 0 to the real value, so the number on screen is a lie for ~700ms. It also animates regardless of the reduce-motion setting. Cost: I cannot tell at a glance whether I am near a limit; I have to wait for the app to finish performing at me. Replace with static text: "12.4 GB of 15 GB". No bar needed. If you keep a bar, it must be a state, not an entrance.
2) The upgrade prompt appearing at three separate gates with three different labels ("Upgrade", "Go Plus", "Unlock more"). Same action, three names — that is a design-token failure in copy. Cost: I stop trusting that "Go Plus" and "Upgrade" are the same door. One gate, one label, one string.
3) The in-app "Manage subscription" link. It deep-links to the store page where I then have to find the subscription again myself. The OS already owns this surface and does it better. Cost: a link that promises management and delivers a scavenger hunt. Remove it; put one line of static text naming where to go.

What I'd keep: the plan explanation — but only as a static screen reachable in two taps, stating what I get and exactly what happens at the limit. That is the one piece of the paywall that answers a real question. Everything else around it is decoration around a decision I already made.

Nothing above needs a redesign. Delete, flatten, relabel."
Jules Park assumes: the sky is not the archive
Jules Park assumes: a setting applies immediately
Mina Sol assumes: a heading is a heading
Mina Sol assumes: a button that looks disabled is disabled
